framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 1H26 total revenue was about THB4.09bn and attributable NPAT about THB596m. The key driver is margin/utilization rather than aggressive balance-sheet growth.
framework.7. Regulation: Food safety, labeling, sugar/excise policy and consumer-health claims affect product economics. Compliance is manageable but sugar-tax changes can influence formulation/mix.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'cash-generative branded beverage with dividend and selective growth'. Sentiment is broadly positive but tied to margins and product momentum.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At 13.20 baht, implied P/E around 13-14x and P/BV around 3x is Fair Value for high ROE/cash returns, with limited room for margin disappointment.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Base: stable domestic demand and healthy margins. Bull: new products/exports drive growth. Bear: category competition and input inflation compress margins.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: category concentration, competition, raw-material/packaging cost, weather, product innovation execution.

stocks.thesis: Brand strength, distribution and manufacturing utilization support cash generation; new products and Indonesia/export growth offer incremental upside.
stocks.bear: Category concentration, aggressive beverage competition, sugar/raw-material costs and weather-sensitive demand can limit growth; premium P/BV leaves less room for execution misses.
stocks.marketBelieves: The market sees ICHI as a high-cash-return beverage brand with good margins but moderate structural growth.
stocks.marketMissing: The market may underprice product innovation/export/Indonesia optionality, while potentially overestimating durability of peak margins.

stocks.debtEbitdaBasis: Hospital: use D/E, cash, EBITDA and capacity utilization

stocks.summary: PR9 remains a high-quality specialist hospital with strong balance sheet. 1H26 NPAT was THB368.8m, down 3.6% YoY, so near-term growth paused despite durable structural demand. Valuation near ~18x P/E is broadly fair rather than cheap.

framework.1. Management: Professional management and a specialist-physician platform support disciplined hospital operations. Capital allocation is conservative; management quality should be judged on specialist recruitment, capacity expansion and return on medical equipment/capex.
framework.2. Product / Moat: PR9 operates a general/tertiary private hospital with strengths in complex care such as heart, kidney, neurology and other specialist services. Moat comes from doctor network, clinical reputation, referrals and patient trust.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thailand private healthcare benefits from aging, chronic disease, insurance and medical tourism. PR9's SAM is narrower than national hospital groups, but specialist intensity and international patients create runway.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Catalysts: international patient growth, specialist-center utilization, higher-acuity mix, new capacity and medical-tourism recovery. Probability medium-high / impact medium-high over 12-36 months.
framework.5. Competitors: Peers include BDMS, BH, BCH and CHG. PR9 has strong quality/financial strength but lower network scale; its edge is focused specialist depth at one flagship hospital.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 1H26 attributable NPAT THB368.8m versus THB382.4m (-3.6% YoY); Q2 NPAT THB184.3m vs THB182.0m. Near-term earnings are stable rather than accelerating.
framework.7. Regulation: Hospital licensing, medical-professional regulation, insurance/third-party payer rules and patient-data privacy matter. Licensing/clinical standards are barriers; reimbursement controls can constrain pricing.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'quality specialist hospital at a reasonable premium'. Sentiment is neutral-to-positive; investors want renewed patient-volume and margin growth.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At the 9-Oct snapshot around THB18.90, valuation is roughly high-teens P/E and ~2.5x P/BV. Fair Value: quality is strong, but a meaningful rerating needs faster earnings growth.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Base: modest patient/mix growth. Bull: international and complex-care ramp drives operating leverage. Bear: flat volumes and rising medical staff costs. 3-5y return comes from earnings growth + modest dividend.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: single-campus concentration, physician retention, international-patient volatility, capex utilization and wage/medical-cost inflation.

stocks.thesis: Complex-care mix, specialist reputation, international patient growth and capacity utilization can support high-quality earnings without balance-sheet stress.
stocks.bear: Single-campus concentration, physician dependence, weaker international mix or delayed capacity ramp can leave earnings flat while the stock still trades at a quality multiple.
stocks.marketBelieves: The market sees PR9 as a high-quality mid-sized private hospital with good margins and balance sheet but slower growth than premium hospital leaders.
stocks.marketMissing: The market may underprice utilization upside from complex-care centers and international patients if capacity ramps, while underestimating single-site concentration.

stocks.debtEbitdaBasis: AMC/collection: Debt/EBITDA N/A; use cash collections, IRR, funding cost, D/E and recovery yield
stocks.debtEbitdaNote: Asset-management economics are driven by cash collection versus portfolio cost and funding cost. Balance-sheet capacity and collection efficiency are more relevant than conventional EBITDA leverage.
stocks.summary: JMT is a scaled distressed-debt operator trading around ~0.55x P/BV after earnings softened. 1H26 NPAT fell ~15.7% YoY to THB486m. Cheap valuation can rerate if cash collections normalize, but recovery quality matters more than headline NPL supply.

framework.1. Management: Founder/group-linked management within the Jaymart ecosystem has deep debt-collection experience. Capital allocation quality is critical because value creation depends on buying portfolios at attractive IRRs, not merely growing receivables.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Businesses include debt collection, purchased NPL management, legal recovery and insurance-related activities. Moat comes from scale, collection/legal infrastructure, data and long recovery experience.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thailand's household/SME NPL pool creates counter-cyclical TAM. Growth runway exists when banks sell more distressed assets, but shareholder value depends on purchase price and collection execution.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Catalysts: stronger cash collections, cheaper portfolio acquisitions, lower funding cost, rising NPL supply and ROE normalization. Probability medium / impact high.
framework.5. Competitors: Peers include BAM and other AMCs. JMT historically delivered stronger private-sector collection efficiency, but current earnings softness has narrowed the perceived premium.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 1H26 NPAT THB486.2m versus THB576.5m (-15.7%); Q2 THB234.0m versus THB246.5m. The key question is collection/recovery economics rather than revenue growth.
framework.7. Regulation: AMC/collection rules, BOT-related debt treatment, consumer protection, debt collection law and legal enforcement affect recovery timing. Regulation creates barriers but can lengthen cash conversion.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'deep-value AMC awaiting collection recovery'. Sentiment is cautious; improvement requires cash collections and ROE rather than simply more NPL purchases.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At ~THB10.10, valuation is roughly mid-teens P/E and ~0.55x P/BV. Cheap if recovery economics normalize; multiple expansion is possible but must be supported by cash collections.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Base: gradual collection recovery. Bull: higher NPL supply bought cheaply + lower funding costs. Bear: weak recovery and impairment keep ROE low. 3-5y value is driven by portfolio IRR spread over funding/collection cost.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: collection shortfall, portfolio mispricing, funding cost/refinancing, accounting estimates/impairment, macro/borrower stress.

stocks.thesis: Structural NPL supply, collection scale and low valuation offer recovery upside if portfolio IRRs and collections improve.
stocks.bear: Weaker collections, expensive historical portfolio purchases, funding cost and accounting complexity can keep ROE depressed and turn low P/BV into a value trap.
stocks.marketBelieves: The market believes JMT is past its high-growth phase and needs to prove collection efficiency and normalized ROE.
stocks.marketMissing: The market may underprice upside from larger distressed-debt supply if JMT can buy at attractive IRRs, while underestimating time-to-cash on existing portfolios.
stocks.variables: Cash collections, debt purchases, recovery yield/IRR, collection cost, funding cost, D/E, ECL/impairment, ROE.
stocks.fit: Contrarian/value investor comfortable with lumpy collections, purchased-debt accounting and credit-cycle risk.
stocks.moatReason: Large collection platform, legal/recovery infrastructure, data/analytics, purchased-debt experience and access to capital create meaningful scale barriers.

framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Base: stable earnings/dividend. Bull: asset monetization + housing recovery. Bear: weak residential demand and low ROE persist. 3-5y return is mostly dividend + modest mean reversion.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: property demand/mortgage rejection, low ROE, asset-value discount persistence, inventory, associate-income volatility.

stocks.bear: Core housing growth is weak; persistent low ROE and asset-heavy capital allocation can justify a permanent discount to book.
stocks.marketBelieves: The market believes QH is cheap for a reason: mature residential operations, low growth and reliance on associate/investment income.
stocks.marketMissing: The market may underprice sum-of-parts value and dividend support if asset monetization/capital returns improve.

framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: holding-company discount, subsidiary earnings volatility, leverage/liquidity, governance/capital allocation, correlated ecosystem stress.

stocks.thesis: JMT recovery, ecosystem restructuring and low holding-company valuation create meaningful rerating optionality.
stocks.bear: Conglomerate complexity, subsidiary leverage, weak cash upstream or renewed losses can keep the holding-company discount wide despite headline profit growth.
stocks.marketBelieves: The market sees JMART as a leveraged ecosystem turnaround whose value is dominated by listed/unlisted subsidiary performance.
stocks.marketMissing: The market may underprice NAV recovery if JMT and other subsidiaries improve simultaneously, but may overstate synergies that do not translate into parent cash flow.
stocks.variables: JMT earnings/collections, Singer/mobile retail results, parent net debt, dividends upstream, NAV discount, equity-method income, liquidity.
stocks.fit: Special-situations/holding-company investor comfortable with conglomerate discount, subsidiary volatility and leverage.

stocks.summary: GFPT is a low-multiple integrated poultry producer. 1H26 NPAT fell ~12.7% YoY to THB1.12bn but remained strong; valuation near ~6x P/E and ~0.6x P/BV provides a substantial margin of safety if poultry spreads stay normal.

framework.1. Management: Family-controlled integrated poultry producer with decades of operating experience. Management's strength is supply-chain integration and export quality; capital allocation is generally conservative.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Integrated poultry chain includes feed, breeding/hatchery, broiler farms, slaughter/processing and cooked-food exports. Moat is moderate through integration, food-safety certifications, export customer relationships and scale.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Global poultry demand grows with affordable protein consumption. Thailand's cooked-chicken export niche offers runway; GFPT can gain through capacity/product mix, though commodity cycles remain.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Catalysts: strong export demand, lower feed costs, chicken-price recovery, capacity utilization and baht competitiveness. Probability medium / impact medium-high.

framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'cheap poultry-cycle value with strong balance sheet'. Sentiment is constructive but investors are wary of peak-cycle earnings.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At THB11.20, P/E ~6.2x and P/BV ~0.62x are cheap. Multiple expansion is possible if earnings prove sustainable rather than cyclical peak.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Base: poultry spreads normalize but remain profitable. Bull: export demand + lower feed costs. Bear: chicken-price decline/feed inflation/disease shock. 3-5y return = normalized earnings + dividends + modest rerating.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: poultry/commodity cycle, feed cost, animal disease, export/trade restrictions, FX and associate earnings.

stocks.marketBelieves: The market believes GFPT earnings are cyclical and current profits may be above normalized levels, justifying a low multiple.
stocks.marketMissing: The market may underprice the quality of integration/export franchise and balance sheet if poultry spreads normalize above historical trough levels.

framework.2. Product / Moat: Operates PT fuel stations plus LPG, logistics and non-oil businesses including Punthai Coffee and customer loyalty ecosystem. Moat is moderate via network density, logistics and customer data/traffic.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thailand fuel retail is mature, but non-oil retail, EV charging, coffee and loyalty monetization expand wallet share. Growth runway is primarily mix shift, not structural fuel-volume growth.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Catalysts: marketing-margin recovery, Punthai/non-oil growth, lower funding cost, capex discipline and OCF conversion. Probability medium / impact high over 6-24 months.

framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'network monetization / non-oil turnaround'. Sentiment is cautious after 1H loss, with improvement dependent on margins and non-oil profitability.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At THB8.30, valuation is better assessed on normalized EBITDA/FCF rather than trailing P/E because 1H26 was loss-making. Fair Value on recovery assumptions, not obviously cheap.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Base: fuel margins normalize and non-oil offsets weakness. Bull: Punthai and customer ecosystem deliver operating leverage. Bear: regulated margins/capex keep ROIC depressed.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: marketing-margin regulation, capex/lease leverage, non-oil execution, EV transition, funding cost and commodity-price volatility.

stocks.thesis: Station density, Max Card ecosystem and non-oil businesses can raise customer monetization and reduce dependence on thin fuel margins; OCF remains supportive.
stocks.bear: Fuel-margin regulation, intense price competition, capex/lease burden and weak non-oil returns can keep ROIC low even with high sales volumes.
stocks.marketBelieves: The market sees PTG as a low-margin fuel retailer trying to become a broader consumer platform; confidence is constrained by earnings volatility.
stocks.marketMissing: The market may underprice the long-term monetization of customer data/non-oil traffic if management can improve return on capital without accelerating leverage.

stocks.summary: DOHOME trades below book around the snapshot and delivered 6M26 NPAT of THB556m. The valuation is undemanding, but earnings remain tied to construction demand, steel/material spreads and inventory productivity.

framework.1. Management: Founder/family-influenced retailer with long experience in building materials and big-box expansion. Management quality is tied to inventory discipline, site selection and leverage control.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Large-format wholesale/retail building materials and home-improvement products. Moat is moderate via assortment, procurement scale, contractor relationships and provincial network.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thailand home-improvement and construction retail remains fragmented. Share-gain runway exists through modern trade penetration, new stores and private-label mix, but macro/housing cycles drive near-term SAM.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Catalysts: construction recovery, same-store sales improvement, gross-margin recovery, lower rates and store maturity. Probability medium / impact medium-high.
framework.5. Competitors: Peers include GLOBAL, HMPRO and other home-improvement retailers. DOHOME is more construction-material/wholesale exposed and more cyclical than HMPRO.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 6M26 total revenue THB16.02bn and NPAT THB556m. Profitability is sensitive to material spreads, mix and store productivity; cash conversion should be tracked with inventory.
framework.7. Regulation: Building codes, product standards, competition law, labor rules and macro credit conditions matter. Regulation is manageable; housing/construction financing is the larger economic constraint.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'cheap cyclical recovery retail'. Sentiment is neutral; investors need proof that demand and margin have bottomed.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At THB3.50, P/E ~16.3x and P/BV ~0.88x. Fair Value: P/BV is cheap, but EBITDA multiple and weak cycle limit immediate rerating.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Base: modest demand recovery with stable margin. Bull: construction upcycle + store maturity. Bear: prolonged weak demand and inventory/price pressure.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: construction/housing downturn, steel/material price swings, inventory, leverage/interest cost and expansion execution.

stocks.thesis: Scale, low P/BV and a normalized construction cycle can drive recovery, while expansion creates long-term share-gain runway.
stocks.bear: Weak construction demand, inventory markdowns, steel-price volatility and debt-funded expansion can keep returns below historical levels.
stocks.marketBelieves: The market views DOHOME as a cyclical building-material retailer with cheap asset valuation but muted near-term demand.
stocks.marketMissing: The market may underprice operating leverage from same-store recovery and procurement/private-label mix once construction demand normalizes.

stocks.summary: MOSHI is one of the stronger late-rank SET100 businesses: 1H26 operating income +17.3%, NPAT +21.5%, GPM 56.4%, 212 stores and positive SSSG. At ~15-16x P/E, valuation is reasonable for its growth/quality.

framework.1. Management: Founder/family-linked specialist retailer with strong execution in merchandising and branch rollout. Management has demonstrated disciplined growth and high margins; alignment is supported by ownership and dividends.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Retail lifestyle/value merchandise under Moshi Moshi. Moat comes from brand, sourcing/merchandising, affordable price points, store productivity and network scale.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thailand lifestyle-value retail is fragmented. MOSHI can gain share through branch expansion, new formats, category extensions and mall/community coverage.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Catalysts: new stores, positive SSSG, margin expansion, product/category innovation and dividend. Probability high / impact high over 12-36 months.
framework.5. Competitors: Competitors include MINISO-like concepts, Daiso/value retailers, department stores and online marketplaces. MOSHI differentiates through local merchandising and strong unit economics.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 1H26 operating income THB1.94bn +17.3% YoY; NPAT THB352.8m +21.5%; GPM rose to 56.4% and SSSG was +3.9%. OCF THB510.5m remained healthy.
framework.7. Regulation: Consumer-product standards, imports, IP/trademark, labor rules and mall leases matter. No major regulatory barrier; execution/sourcing is the bigger moat.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'specialty retail compounder'. Sentiment is positive with improving margins and expansion, though investors watch valuation and SSSG sustainability.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At THB34.50, valuation is roughly mid-teens P/E, ~4.3x P/BV and ~9-10x EV/EBITDA. Fair Value to slightly attractive for 20%+ profit growth and strong ROE.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Base: mid/high-teens earnings growth via stores + SSSG. Bull: sustained margin and new-format success. Bear: saturation/weak SSSG. 3-5y return is mostly earnings compounding + dividend.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: store saturation, merchandising miss, sourcing/FX, mall-rent inflation, e-commerce substitution.

stocks.thesis: High store economics, branch runway, strong margins and consistent cash flow can compound earnings at attractive rates.
stocks.bear: Rapid expansion can saturate locations, fashion/lifestyle demand can shift, and high P/BV leaves downside if SSSG or margins disappoint.
stocks.marketBelieves: The market sees MOSHI as a high-quality specialty retailer with visible branch expansion and strong margins.
stocks.marketMissing: The market may still underprice long runway from new formats/categories and operating leverage if SSSG stays positive, but current quality is no longer hidden.
stocks.variables: Store count, SSSG, sales/sqm, gross margin, inventory turns, OCF, new-format productivity, dividend payout.
stocks.fit: Quality-growth investor willing to pay a moderate premium for high ROE, cash flow and store runway.
stocks.moatReason: Distinct lifestyle-value positioning, fast merchandising, sourcing scale, brand recognition and a rapidly expanding store network create a meaningful retail moat in a fragmented niche.

stocks.summary: AAV retains a strong low-cost airline franchise, but 1H26 swung to a THB1.49bn loss from THB1.60bn profit as fuel and FX pressure overwhelmed fare gains. The equity is an operational turnaround with significant leverage risk.

framework.1. Management: Founder/executive leadership has deep low-cost aviation experience, backed by the wider AirAsia ecosystem. Management quality is proven operationally, but balance-sheet risk management is equally important.
framework.2. Product / Moat: AAV is the holding company for Thai AirAsia. Moat comes from AirAsia brand, route density, low-cost culture, digital distribution, regional network and airport slots.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Asian short-haul travel has structural growth from tourism and rising mobility. AAV's growth runway exists across domestic/ASEAN/South Asia, but profitability depends on fuel, FX and capacity discipline.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Catalysts: lower jet fuel, stronger baht, tourism recovery, higher fares/load factors, fleet utilization and refinancing. Probability medium / impact very high.
framework.5. Competitors: Peers include other Thai airlines and regional low-cost carriers. AirAsia has stronger LCC brand/network, but leverage remains a key disadvantage.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 6M26 revenue THB24.55bn vs THB25.03bn and net loss THB1.49bn vs THB1.60bn profit. Q2 core loss was severe as jet fuel surged; OCF turned negative.
framework.7. Regulation: Aviation licenses, slot allocation, safety regulation, fuel/airport taxes and bilateral traffic rights matter. Regulation is a barrier but also creates fixed costs.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'high-beta airline recovery'. Sentiment is negative/fragile during fuel shock; it can reverse quickly if fuel and FX normalize.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At THB0.84, P/BV is below 1x but earnings are negative and leverage is high. Fair Value only on recovery assumptions; balance-sheet risk prevents a simple 'cheap' label.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Base: fares/traffic offset part of fuel pressure. Bull: fuel falls + baht strengthens + tourism remains robust. Bear: prolonged fuel shock and refinancing stress. Equity return is highly convex.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: fuel price, FX, leverage/liquidity, tourism/geopolitical shock, aircraft/lease obligations and capacity execution.

stocks.thesis: AirAsia network/brand, stronger fares and tourism demand can create high operating leverage when fuel/FX normalize.
stocks.bear: High D/E, fuel-price shocks, FX losses, lease obligations and weak load factor can rapidly destroy equity value even with strong passenger demand.
stocks.marketBelieves: The market views AAV as a leveraged tourism/fuel beta rather than a stable compounder.
stocks.marketMissing: The market may underprice recovery leverage if fuel prices and baht normalize, but may also underestimate how quickly liquidity can deteriorate in an adverse shock.
stocks.variables: Fuel price/hedge, THB/USD, passengers, load factor, fare/RASK, CASK ex-fuel, fleet utilization, OCF, D/E, liquidity and aircraft leases.
stocks.fit: High-risk cyclical/tourism investor comfortable with fuel, FX, leverage and airline volatility.
stocks.moatReason: AirAsia brand, regional route network, low-cost operating model, slots/hubs and group ecosystem create meaningful commercial advantages, but airline economics remain structurally cyclical and capital intensive.

stocks.summary: GST—renamed from THCOM—has a real regulated infrastructure moat and returned to strong 1H26 profit of THB500m from a prior-year loss. However, a large part of the improvement came from other income, so core recurring earnings must be separated from headline profit.

framework.1. Management: Renamed from THCOM after strategic ownership/positioning changes. Management operates a technically complex satellite platform; shareholder alignment now depends on disciplined investment within the broader Gulf ecosystem.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Businesses include satellite and related services, internet/media, overseas telecom and joint ventures. Moat is strong from licenses/orbital rights, infrastructure, engineering and customer relationships.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Regional connectivity, satellite broadband, enterprise/government services and space infrastructure offer long-run TAM. Growth requires successful next-generation satellite/capacity investment and commercialization.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Catalysts: new satellite projects, government/enterprise contracts, Gulf ecosystem synergies, regulatory clarity and recurring EBITDA growth. Probability medium / impact high.
framework.5. Competitors: Competitors include regional/global satellite operators and terrestrial broadband alternatives. GST has domestic strategic positioning but faces technology substitution and scale competition.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 6M26 total revenue THB1.54bn +11.6%, but revenue from operations fell to THB950m; NPAT improved to THB500m from -THB88m largely with higher other income. OCF THB234m and D/E 0.63x.
framework.7. Regulation: Orbital slots, spectrum, satellite licenses, concession/contract obligations, cybersecurity and telecom regulation are central. Regulation is a major barrier to entry and a key thesis risk.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'THCOM transformed into Gulf Space Technology'. Sentiment is improving on strategic optionality, but core earnings quality remains under scrutiny.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At ~THB9.50, valuation is around mid-teens P/E and ~1x P/BV. Fair Value given regulated-asset moat, but upside requires recurring core growth rather than one-off income.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Base: stable legacy cash flows + selective new-space investment. Bull: successful new satellite/strategic contracts. Bear: capex-heavy projects, regulatory/legal setbacks or weak core revenue.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: regulatory/concession disputes, capex/project returns, technology substitution, customer concentration, core-vs-one-off earnings quality.

stocks.thesis: Satellite rights, technical know-how and strategic Gulf ecosystem can support a new growth phase in space/digital infrastructure.
stocks.bear: Core operating revenue declined in 1H26 and headline profit benefited from other income; satellite replacement capex, regulatory disputes and project returns remain significant risks.
stocks.marketBelieves: The market sees GST as a strategic Gulf-linked space/satellite platform rather than the old mature THCOM story.
stocks.marketMissing: The market may underprice strategic optionality in new satellite/space infrastructure, while overpricing one-off profit if recurring core economics remain weak.
